vocabulary.definition: "Barking" is the sound that a dog makes, usually when the dog is angry. If we say that a person "barks out" something, it means that they are angry and yelling at someone. They are kind of like an angry dog in that moment.

A person who is "homophobic" is someone who doesn't like "gay people". The word "phobic" means "afraid". I don't think homophobic people are really afraid of gay people but they certainly don't like them. It is a very negative word to be homophobic. It's like a kind of uneducated low class thing to be.
Someone who is "intoxicated" is either drunk or "messed up" on some drugs. People do weird things when they are "intoxicated". I'm sure you aren't surprised.

A "heckler" is a term that is used to describe someone in the audience who is shouting out comments to bother the people acting or doing some sport. They are in sporting events and comedy clubs. They could be at plays too but they would be kicked out quickly.
If you "get under someone's skin" it means that you make them very angry and irritate them. You make them bothered by every little thing you do and say.

If you "lose your cool" it means that you lose your temper. You get angry and bark at someone. He lost his cool at work yesterday because he didn't sleep for a few days. He yelled at his boss over the tiniest thing. I've never seen him like that before but I'll have to admit it was pretty funny.

A "split second" is a common term in English. It literally means, "less than one second" but often is used to mean a very short time. After she heard that her husband went to the hospital she raced over there in a split second to see him.
